subject: retired racehorses
one_liner: Settle up with the other horses in your field. Publicly, in oats or dollars, whether or not anyone asked.
brand_voice_notes: Payments infrastructure that speaks like a racing secretary reading results over a PA. Every number is announced. Nothing is private, because privacy was never built. Deadpan, procedural, faintly institutional. Copy behaves as if a horse having a checking account is the settled part and the interesting question is fee structure.

hero.h1: Every horse owes another horse something.
hero.sub: Furlong settles debts between retired racehorses and posts the result to the paddock feed within four seconds. There is no private mode. There was going to be one.

features.title: Public by default, permanently
features.blurb: Each settlement posts to the feed the whole barn reads: payer, payee, amount, memo. The visibility toggle exists in the settings screen and has never once changed anything. We left it in because removing it required a migration.

features.title: Split by distance travelled
features.blurb: Furlong divides a shared bill by how far each horse walked to reach the thing being paid for, measured in furlongs, rounded up. The horse nearest the hay pays least. This has restructured the social order of nine separate farms and we are watching closely.

features.title: Hoof ID
features.blurb: Biometric authentication from a single front hoof pressed to the reader plate. Median time to authenticate is 41 minutes, most of which is convincing the horse. Once in, the session lasts eleven months.

demo_screen_concept: The Furlong paddock feed rendered as a totalisator board: a dark tote-green ledger where each row is one horse-to-horse payment, showing an avatar, payer arrow payee, a deadpan memo ('farrier, split 3 ways'), amber split-flap amounts, and like/nudge counts. A left rail filters the feed (All / Barn 7 / Owed to me / Settled), a header shows running balance and outstanding debts in amber LED numerals that tick when the filter changes, each row expands to reveal the distance-split breakdown per horse in furlongs, and a 'request' modal lets you dun another horse for a specific amount with a memo, which then posts to the top of the feed.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the tote-board direction is pure display typography and a photograph behind the results board would fight it. Demo subject assets skipped as a separate slot: the feed is a ledger, not a photo surface, but its rows carry avatars, so the whole budget went to four square deadpan horse portraits that do double duty as the landing page's three testimonial headshots and as the demo feed's avatar set.

items.prompt: Editorial photograph: a corporate staff-portrait headshot of a retired chestnut racehorse mare, mid-teens, facing the camera squarely with a flat neutral expression, slightly unkempt forelock, faint white star on the forehead, ears neutral. Lighting and palette: deep paddock-night green backdrop #0D1712, warm amber key light #F5B32C raking from the left, bone-white #EAE6DA highlights on the coat. Muted, institutional, low-saturation. Editorial photograph, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, single subject centered, square crop, head and upper neck only, framed like a corporate staff portrait. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no signage, no rendered UI screens or interfaces anywhere in the frame.

Editorial photograph: a corporate staff-portrait headshot of a dark bay racehorse gelding, lean and alert, mane neatly braided, facing the camera with an appraising expression, muscular neck, no tack or bridle. Same paddock-night green backdrop #0D1712, amber key light #F5B32C, bone highlights, 85mm, square crop. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI.

Editorial photograph: a corporate staff-portrait headshot of an older dappled grey broodmare, calm and heavy-lidded, soft whiskered muzzle, facing the camera three-quarters, dignified and slightly bored. Same paddock-night green backdrop #0D1712, amber key light #F5B32C, bone highlights, 85mm, square crop. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI.

Editorial photograph: a corporate staff-portrait headshot of a bay racehorse with a wide white blaze down the face, one ear tipped sideways, looking just off-camera as if waiting to be told a meeting has started. Same paddock-night green backdrop #0D1712, amber key light #F5B32C, bone highlights, 85mm, square crop. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI.

design_direction.style: Totalisator board terminal: a racetrack tote display used as a payments UI. Condensed racing-form display type, amber split-flap numerals on paddock-night green, hairline brass rules, tabular figures everywhere, no rounded friendliness.
design_direction.archetype: Consumer payments app staged as a racetrack totalisator board: results-board hero with a live-ticking ledger strip, feature rows set like race conditions, pricing as three claiming classes, footer as a chart footnote.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Split-flap digit flips on numerals (150ms, staggered 40ms), amber row highlight sweeps on hover, no easing softer than ease-out, nothing bounces. Reduced-motion disables all flips and shows final values.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-width board header with brass hairline rules top and bottom. Left two-thirds: condensed uppercase H1 at 1.5em line-height 0.95, sub in IBM Plex Sans at 18px. Right third: a live results panel listing four recent settlements in tabular amber figures, updating on an interval. Primary CTA is a hard-edged amber block, secondary is an underlined bone-colored text link.
